To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lowbush (Vaccinium) cranberry acts through the DAF-16/FoxO pathway to promote lifespan extension and axon branching changes in aging C. elegans posterior touch receptor neurons.

the lowbush cranberries increase lifespan and axon branch numbers in aging C. elegans, through the DAF-16 pathway, and this pathway is not activated upon consumption of other functional foods that impact C. elegans aging.

lowbush berry supplementation activates the aging-related transcription factor, DAF-16, in the nervous system of the nematode, C. elegans, and that DAF-16 activation is necessary for the lifespan and neuronal morphological effects of lowbush berry treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the mechanisms by which berry consumption impacts aging and the aging nervous system.
the cellular mechanisms that underlie the health benefits of berry consumption and the role of DAF- 16/FOXO transcription factor in the aging process.
the cellular mechanisms underlying lifespan extension and neuronal plasticity, and the potential of berry consumption to impact healthspan.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DAF-16 nuclear localization in aging worms is not a universal indicator of lifespan extension.
the lowbush cranberries are a potent anti-aging compound and that DAF-16 plays a role in its anti-aging effects.
DAF-16 activation is required for the effects of lowbush cranberries on lifespan and touch receptor neuron aging.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lowbush berries act through DAF- 16/FOXO to promote increased lifespan, improved mechanosensory ability, and axon branching changes in aging posterior touch neurons.

lowbush berry treatment induces DAF-16 signaling in aging C. elegans to promote increased lifespan, improved mechanosensory function and posterior touch receptor axon branching, but that DAF-16 induction may be a specific mechanism of lowbush berry supplementation, rather than a universal mechanism of berry supplementation.
lowbush berries act through DAF- 16 signaling in C. elegans to promote increased lifespan, axon branching in posterior touch receptor neurons, and mechanosensation in aged worms.
The main takeaway from our work is that

lowbush berry supplementation can activate DAF-16, which can promote lifespan extension and axon morphological changes in aged touch receptor neurons, but this may not be the mechanism underlying the lifespan extension effects of all berry treatments.
lowbush berry consumption promotes lifespan extension in C. elegans and this is dependent on the transcription factor DAF16.
the effects of lowbush cranberries on aging and neuronal function are mediated by DAF-16.
